# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS (use these instead of the source text)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "Frank Merriwell's Support; Or, A Triple Play" by Burt L. Standish (1901, Street & Smith; Gutenberg #62719)

**Core cast:** Frank Merriwell (Yale pitcher, ex-Yale; wrist sprained, can't use "double-shoot" reliably; later "reverse curve"), Dick Merriwell (younger half-brother, ~14, pitcher/shortstop, has "jump ball," can throw left/right; homesick for Felicia, Lake Sunshine, Pleasant Valley), Old Joe Crowfoot (Indian, dirty red blanket, black pipe, speaks broken English "Heap big," "Injun Heart" = Dick, "Steady Hand" = Frank; wounded earlier, shot; loves Dick; carries hidden knife), Bart Hodge (catcher), Jack Ready (3rd base, jokey, "Ye gods"), Harry Rattleton (2nd base, mangled words, "dim-jandy"), Bruce Browning (1st base, big, lazy), Berlin Carson (rf/ss), Greg Carker (socialist talk, "earthquake"), Joe Gamp (New Hampshire, stutters, center field, huge catch), John Swiftwing (Indian, lf, former Carlisle), Dick, Felicia (Dick's sweetheart, Little Star Eyes; father Mr. Delores, Spanish refugee).

**Antagonists:** Omaha Stars (Dorrity captain/1st base, Batch pitcher, Hanson catcher, Jack 2b, Maloney rf, Corrigan 3b, Teller cf, Skew ss, O'Grady lf, manager Wilson). Umpire Jim Derring (corrupt; bribed by gambler Hazen, the red-faced stout man with stubby mustache; Wescott, a man in blue, partner bettor). Derring is mobbed; Morrisy replaces him.

**Game 1 (Omaha):** Merries lose 3–2 in 9th after Frank's wrist injured; Frank pitches 7th; crowd turns against umpire; Frank protects umpire from mob; Dorrity agrees to new umpire; Frank refuses forfeit; Merries lose to bad support (Teller muffed/caught-fly dispute; Corrigan scores winning run). Hazen offered Frank $50→$100→$200 to throw game; Frank flung money back; Hazen grabbed him; Frank shook him; Hazen's pistol knocked away by Frank's boot; Frank returned revolver empty. Frank challenges Stars to rematch.
- Dick arrives Omaha with Old Joe. Frank promises Joe shelter/tobacco; Joe agrees to stay near Dick. Dick bets $1000 with Hazen; Frank makes him donate winnings to charity; Dick must give money to hotel proprietor.
- **Game 2 (Omaha rematch):** Dick pitches, fields brilliantly (catches two line drives), strikes out many; Merries win 1–0 (Dick's hit with Ready, Dick stole bases). Hazen loses bets.

**Minneapolis/St. Paul (Ch. X–XIII):** Merries watch St. Paul vs Minneapolis; St. Paul pitcher Foley spiked by Prince (Minneapolis). Captain Trueman of St. Paul; "jay pitcher" = Frank in disguise (carrot hair, derby hat, bagging trousers, idiot grin, Mud Creek / Slabtown / Suckerville claims, "a-haw! a-haw!"). Stammering friend Joe on bleachers (Bill = jay's name in dialogue). Jay uses "double-shoot" revealed as the "in and out" curve. Jay hits home run, St. Paul ties; Old Joe performs war-whoop; jay's Yale friends sing; St. Paul wins. Gamblers Charley Bates (ex-millionaire, opium fiend) and Hank Dowling (gambler) bribe via waiter Pete (drugs vichy water). Frank fails to pitch; Dick pitches with jump ball; Frank's home run wins 2–1; Dowling loses $800 (or so). Dowling also punched by Frank's disguise; friends rush; Frank fights ruffians; Yale cheer "Breka Co ax" song ("Here's to good old Merry").

**Philadelphia (Ch. XIX–XX):** Nick Robinson (Athletic manager) challenges Merries; Jack Wilder. Frank doesn't drink/smoke. Squinty Jim McCann (bully) and urchins taunt Old Joe ("Dogs!"); Dick thrashes Jim; Jim's brother Bud McCann (prize-fighter/catcher) vows revenge. Policeman thanks Frank (his son Bob reformed through Frank). Athletic game: Frank pitches; Bud throws bat trip Frank; fight; Gamp's catch; Dick slides; Dick triple-plays unassisted (Ch. XXV Frank says "Dick's triple play" — actually Dick catches liner, steps to 2nd, tags Robinson); Merries lead 5–4. McCann spikes/knees Dick (face bloodied); Frank beats McCann. Old Joe arrives to inspire Browning's hit; Frank's hit; Merries win.

**Hazard challenge (Ch. XXVI–XXIX):** Jack Hazard (white hair, youthful face) challenges at Polo Grounds, team "The Mysteries" of Frank's Yale friends: Gene Skelding (3b, reformed), Starbright (1b), Mason (ss), Oliver Packard (2b), Dismal Jones (lf), Hans Dunnerwurst (rf, German), Barney Mulloy (catcher, Irish), Ephraim Gallup (cf, farm boy), Dade Morgan (pitcher, captain). Frank sends Dick to pitch; Yale men bet vs Dick; Inza Burrage and Elsie Bellwood (Bart's sweetheart) present. Old Joe kills rabid dog (Nero, St. Bernard owner's dog) with knife; owner threatens. Dick homesick (Felicia). Dick wins 3–2... final: Dick steals home for winning run in 9th; Merries win (score tied 5–5 earlier? final: Merries 6–5 approx). Inza gives Dick Yale-blue badge.

**Ending:** "No. 76 of the Merriwell Series, Dick Merriwell at Fardale" advertisement.

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Betty Wales, Junior: A Story for Girls" by Margaret Warde (Edith Kellogg Dunton) (1906, Penn Publishing; Gutenberg #64033)

**Setting:** Harding College (fictional). Belden House; Room 27 (Betty's "single," Belden, 3rd floor? she had 27 Belden); Chapin House (former freshman home). Hilton House, Westcott House, Main Building, Cuyler's (tea-room/restaurant), Holmes's, Paradise pond, Clio Club, Dramatic Club, Argus (college magazine).

**Main characters:**
- **Betty Wales** (narrator focus; blonde yellow curls; "Power behind the Throne"; unimaginative; cousin Lucile Merrifield freshman; brother Will, sister Nan, "Little Sister" (smallest sister); parents Mr. & Mrs. Wales from Cleveland; father gives Nassau invitation, trip to West Indies).
- **"The Merry Hearts"** club (founded in Ch. II, pin, president Mary Brooks [senior, Argus editor, romanticist, "Mary-Bird-Club"], secretary Madeline Ayres [Bohemian, French, second self "Georgia Ames"; from "Bohemia, New York"; biology/mushrooms; Miss Stevens botany assistant]).
- **The B's:** Babbie Hildreth (smile, chafing-dish with copper rabbits, rich, maid stipend), Babe (Bab? "Babe" = Mabel? no: Babe), Bob Parker (zoology, toads, grasshoppers, basket-ball, tomboy, night-watchman feud; Henry the night-watchman).
- Katherine Kittredge ("K.", canvas bag, basket-ball, father has five hungry mouths, Kankakee), Rachel Morrison (class president, tutors freshmen, little white house around corner, junior president, later senior president), Roberta Lewis (shy writer, pseudonym "Georgia Ames" author, Mary's idol, cousin from Boston), Helen Chase Adams (formerly lonely roommate; "prod."; Philosophical Club; joins Argus; "Mrs. Erasmus J. Ames" letter), Nita Reese (Hilton House, post-card collection, "aunt"), Eleanor Watson (outcast after sophomore story scandal; Judge Watson; step-brother Jim; Aunt Flo; resigned Dramatic Club; joins Merry Hearts at end), Dora Carlson (Eleanor's freshman; father injured; barn burned; works as waitress at Mrs. Tait's), Christy Mason (Argus business manager), Lucile (cousin), Alice Waite (two men, Tom Alison), Jean Eastman (snide), Marion Lawrence ("Laurie"), Marion Lustig, Emily Davis, Jane Drew, Miss Ferris, Miss Stuart (dean), Miss Raymond (theme course), Miss Case (rich lonely), Miss Ray, Lotta Gardner, Ethel Hale (teacher; chaperon; engaged to Eaton), Dr. John Elliot Eaton (associate prof English; "English Essayists"; ten-minute tests; blasé; horse; later honorary Merry Heart; Yale-friend of Tom/John Alison; book written; moves to New York), Professor Hinsdale (Dr.), Professor Jones (botany), Professor Lawrence, Mrs. Kent & Miss Andrews (Belden house mother/teacher), Annie (Irish maid), Martha (Nassau cocoanut-cake seller), Tom Alison & John Alison (Yale brothers; John = Eaton's college chum; railroad in New Mexico; Tombstone letter).

**Key events in order:**
1. Opening (Ch I): Betty in single room, Mary arrives; Lucile arrives; Katherine, Rachel, Roberta arrive; Madeline "Toss it over, please." T. Reed's room offered to Lucile.
2. Ch II: Merry Hearts formed in 27 Belden; name suggested by Roberta; object = making others have good times; Madeline's "Bohemian" spirit; Student's Aid Fair mentioned.
3. Ch III: Dr. Eaton lectures; Madeline submits Georgia Ames theme ("Matthew Arnold and the Ten-Minute Test") on Helen's paper; Eaton praises it. Bob's toads and grasshoppers.
4. Ch IV: Roberta learns of Georgia; Argus submission rejected by Mary (poem "Song of Sleep"); Georgia story read; Roberta reveals she wrote Georgia's pieces.
5. Ch V: Mushroom party (inky drippers/coprinus, puff-balls); Georgia admitted to Merry Hearts; "Power Behind the Throne" nickname.
6. Ch VI: Georgia's style: calling cards, violets ($3.80), Nita's post-card ("Try Georgiana Arms"), Mrs. Erasmus J. Ames letter from Eaton.
7. Ch VII: Dora's tears; Japanese tea for Harding Aid/Dora; Madeline's Japanese play; Christy Mason's cousin; Dora's sophomore year funded.
8. Ch VIII: Faculty party; Eaton talks with Betty (thinks Betty = Georgia); Alice Waite & Tom Alison concert; Tom sends Huyler's and Yale prom invitation.
9. Ch IX: Eaton asks for Georgia after class; Georgia "dies" (Arizona, pneumonia, Tombstone) letter; Betty tells Eaton about Mrs. Ames; Eaton gracious.
10. Ch X: Christmas; Tom's letter reveals John Alison sent picture/note to Eaton; Betty confesses to Eaton; Eaton made honorary member.
11. Ch XI: Janitor/clock-tower; Bob as ghost; Miss Stuart; Miss Case joins; Ethel found crying; Nassau invitation from Dr. Eaton's father's letter; Helen's Nassau.
12. Ch XII: Library fire; Bob leads book-passing; Eleanor invited to trip; Eleanor Merry Heart election later.
13. Ch XIII–XIV: Nassau trip; Dr. Eaton appears on ship; Ethel seasick; divers for pennies; Grant's Town; Easter tree; orange rolling; Ethel & Eaton lost in Grant's Town.
14. Ch XV: Betty nearly drowns at Hog Island; Eaton rescues her; Ethel calls him "John."
15. Ch XVI–XVIII: Return; Eleanor rejected for Merry Hearts (later accepted); prom; Eleanor escorts Jim; Helen's Argus election; dress reform (simple dresses, $7 frocks); Ethel announces engagement to Eaton (Ethel was Eaton's freshman prom date; agreed to decide during year).
16. Ch XIX: Commencement; Rachel's speech; donor (Eaton) gives $50,000 with ten thousand for junior class vote; Madeline graduates early option; Georgia "found" as freshman entrance candidate; Merry Hearts sing "Here's to Betty Wales."
